changes: Lock the band slot at open to the tallest words it can turn into (cancelled, order today, no signal, tomorrow), not just the words showing at open. If anything has to give, shorten the name with an ellipsis. Never clip 'Do not prep', 'Order today' or '+1 more this week'. Test a name of about 30 characters cancelled while Prep is open, at default, large and extra-large text.

On Home, answer Got it without covering the next heads-up card. Either answer in the card's own place (C's original in-place words) or lift the slip clear. Then measure that the next card's Got it and Open the function are fully visible at 390.

Before ready, run the click tests the spec names. First, the header-height test with Prep open through a booking, signal off, 23:59:30 to 00:00:30 Queensland and a cancel. Second, two staff on one tablet for the per-person Got it key.
Remeasure in the implemented app at 390, 768 and 1280 with stand-in fonts, the head chef's cut-off bar and large text: Prep rows, the slot height and Home's first screen. All mix numbers are Preview.
Keep at least 8 px between '+1 more this week' and the minus and the top bar chips above them. A stray tap aimed at the chef hat or bell should not open #/fn or hide the line mid-service.

Head chef's choice I would still put to him (not a blocker): for a person who has tapped Got it, the work-page line could step aside. This is decided when the page opens or unlocks, never live. It gives the prep row back without a daily minus tap.
newRisks: The locked slot clips its own warning words. Reproduced in the preview: prep.html at 390, using my in-browser probe with no file changed. A function renamed 'Henderson and Nguyen engagement' and cancelled while Prep is open needs 90 px inside the 50 px slot. The overflow: hidden cuts 'Do not prep' (drawn at 107 to 147 px, slot ends at 114) and the bottom of '+1 more this week'. Large text: 125 px of words in a 79 px slot. Extra-large: 138 px in 87 px. Single A grew instead (the row-shift risk); this clipping is new with the mix's height lock.

The slip covers the next heads-up. Reproduced in the preview: home.html at 390, after Got it on Smith 60th. The slip at 709 to 776 px covers the bottom 18 px of the Jones card's 48 px Got it (679 to 727 px) and the lower half of Open the function (681 to 725 px). A low wet-finger tap lands on the slip and does nothing. C answered in place. Moving the card under Your day put the next Got it right in the slip's band.

A tablet left on Prep: under open-only, a short-notice booking shows only as quiet-paper 'Order today' words in the 50 px slot. The charcoal band appears only when Prep is opened again, which could be after the whole service. The words are checked in the preview (s-booking-after). Whether people notice them on a busy tablet is Risk / Not evidenced.

Words change under a finger: the slot's words switch from Smith 60th to 'Order today · Lee engagement' while open, so a tap aimed at Smith opens Lee's sheet. It is read only and one Close fixes it. Risk / Not evidenced.
contractFit:
Needs work.

text:
Cook mid-service, the mix: 8.5 (A 6, B 4, C 8). Endorse with changes.

Coherent: one function piece per page. Home keeps Your day first, shows every fact at 0 taps, and a reflex Got it leaves a line, not nothing. Open-only holds the first prep row at 313 px through a booking, lost signal, midnight and a cancel (16 checks, Preview). It beats C because it reaches every work page. Cost: one prep row on band-empty days (6 to 5), and no coworkers on Home's first screen until Got it.

New faults, Reproduced in the preview (my probe, 390):
1. The locked slot clips. A long-named function cancelled while Prep is open needs 90 px in 50 px; "Do not prep" is cut. Same at large and extra-large text.
2. After the first Got it, the slip covers the bottom 18 px of the next card's Got it.

Changes: lock the slot at the tallest words it can become, never clip Do not prep or Order today; keep the slip clear of the next Got it; test long names and text sizes; remeasure in the implemented app. I still prefer the line stepping aside after Got it.

Contract fit: Needs work. Clipped status words; Home order and the lost row need the head chef.

changes: Cap the open-only lock. A shared tablet left on Prep may not reopen Prep all service, so today's band (a same-day booking, its rounds, In 10 min) must appear at a safe moment, such as after [60 s] with no touch or at the next route change. Draw that frame and add it to the header-height click test.
Design the busy-week card (3 or more functions in the week, one Got it) before the Home card pull request ships, not leave it open. Christmas weeks would otherwise mean 5 or 6 Got its in a row.

Keep the next card's Got it clear of the Undo slip. In home-after-390.png the slip covers the lower part of the Jones wedding Got it. Scroll the next card so its Got it sits above the slip, or answer in the line itself.
On a shared device the work-page minus resets when a different person signs in (the spec's own option), so one cook's hide does not take the line from the next.
Plainer card name: 'Function this week' and 'Function tomorrow' instead of 'Function heads-up'. Check it with a new starter.
Ship the work-page line (build step 3, tests first) before the Home card (step 2). It fixes my actual Tuesday problem, a function nowhere on Prep.
newRisks: Frozen slot holds back today's band. The open-only rule now covers the band's own slot, so on a Prep screen left open (shared tablet), a same-day booking's rounds, In 10 min and the pinned strip show only as words in a 50 px quiet line until Prep is opened again. Risk / Not evidenced. Only the short-notice Order today words were checked (mix preview, measurements.json openOnly prep-390-booking); a same-day booking was not drawn.

The Undo slip after the first Got it covers the lower part of the next card's Got it button at 390, so a quick second tap can land on the slip. Reproduced in the preview (shots/home-after-390.png). New, because C answered in the card's own place.

Two ways to put it away: Got it on Home is per person, the minus on work pages is per phone. A new starter may confuse them, and on a shared tablet the minus hides the line for the next person that day. Risk / Not evidenced. Only the words and spoken labels were checked in the mix preview (measurements.json minus.spokenLabel, gotIt slip words).

The team board stays off the first screen through up to two Got its (On with you at 737 px, then 780 px, with 0 of 5 coworker rows). Checked in the mix preview (measurements.json gotIt). This is a cost similar to C's, and it ends after the last Got it (460 px, 5 of 5).
contractFit: Needs work. Surface purpose works: the card is quiet paper with the steel edge, the line is quiet reference paper, never charcoal or amber, and the Order today and Not ordered yet tags use ink words (13.48:1). State words work: Got it is never shown as Saved, and Cancelled uses a plain .btn. Two things need the head chef's OK: the card sits between Your day and On with you until Got it (a departure from staff-first), and Prep drops from 6 to 5 rows at 390 on days with no band. Not evidenced: focus rings, dark mode, large text, roles (signed out, Functions only), loading and failed read, Rescheduled, the head chef's cut-off bar with the line, per-staff Got it keys, and the midnight repaint.
text:
Mix 8 (A 7, C 6, B 4). Coherent: one slot under Your day that starts as C's card and folds in place to A's line, the same line in the band's empty slot, B's tag in the stock line. It beats A: every fact at 0 taps once per person, a function on every work page all week, and the open-only rule closes A's moving-row risk (0 px in 16 Preview checks).

Endorse with changes:
1. Cap the open-only lock. A tablet left on Prep may never reopen it. Today's band (same-day booking, rounds) must appear at a safe moment, such as after [60 s] untouched. Test it.
2. Design the busy-week card (3 or more functions, one Got it) first.
3. Keep the next Got it clear of the Undo slip.
4. The minus resets for a different person on a shared device.
5. Plainer name: Function this week.
6. Ship the work-page line before the card.

New failure paths: frozen slot holds back today's band (Risk, Not evidenced); slip covers the next Got it at 390 (Reproduced, home-after-390.png); Got it and minus confused (Risk; words checked in mix preview).

Contract fit: Needs work. Surfaces and words fit. Home order and the lost row need my OK; focus, dark, large text, roles, midnight Not evidenced.

bestSingle: A, Fill the gap (my round 2 score 7; C 5, B 4)
changes: Fixed-height slot must never clip. Put the words people must read (Cancelled · Do not prep, Order today, No signal) in the one-line nowrap label row, cut the name short with an ellipsis on line 2, and add a click test at 390 with a name of 40 or more characters and the large text setting.

Answer Got it in the place of the collapsed line, using C's in-place words with Undo, instead of the bottom slip. Otherwise keep the next card's Got it and Open the function clear of the slip. Measure it at 390 x 844.

Drop the Tomorrow heads-up card for anyone who tapped Got it on the week card. The Home line already says Tomorrow and the band covers the work pages. Keep the full card with a Tomorrow tag for people who never tapped. This cuts Ann's added taps this week from 4 to 2.

Keep 'Cancelled · Do not prep' on the work-page line and the Home line until the function's date passes, not only for the rest of the day it was cancelled. The line also told people who never tapped Got it.
Design and measure the combined card for a week with 3 or more functions before the Home card pull request (build step 2), not after the head chef chooses.

Build step 3's open-only test must run the app's real paint() with the stand-in listener and clock: a booking, going offline, 23:59:30 to 00:00:30 Queensland, and a cancellation. The preview's template swap does not count.
newRisks: Reproduced (design-mix/prep.html, 390 x 844; a made-up 37-character name 'Robertson and Nguyen engagement party' run through fmaSim('booking') and fmaSim('cancelled')): the slot is locked at 50 px and the words need 90 px. Because the slot has overflow: hidden, the end of the text is cut off, including 'Do not prep' (the text ends at 148 px, the slot at 114 px). In A the line grew taller, so this failure is new to the open-only blend. Repair: change 1.

Reproduced (design-mix/home.html, 390 x 844, after Got it on Smith 60th): the bottom slip (709 to 776 px) covers the lower 18 of the 48 px of the Jones card's Got it (679 to 727) and Open the function (681 to 725). Undo (x 308 to 380, y 722 to 766) overlaps the corner of Open the function, so a tap there lands on the slip or on Undo. C answered in the card's own place and A had no second card, so this is new to the mix. Repair: change 2.

Risk / Not evidenced: the red Cancelled card on Home goes only to people who tapped Got it, but the work-page line has already told everyone. A cook who saw the line on Monday and is off on the day it was cancelled later finds the line has moved on to the next function with no word about the cancellation. C's 'only people who were told' rule assumed the card was the only way to be told. Repair: change 4.

Risk / Not evidenced: the open-only lock was tested only by swapping words in a static page (16 checks with simulated data). The app's paint(), listener metadata, the clock repaint and the large text setting were not run, and the words have 1 px to spare (49 px in a 50 px slot) with the preview fonts.
contractFit: Needs work. Works: the surfaces (the line on quiet reference paper, the card on paper with a steel edge, upcoming functions never charcoal or amber); no new reads, rules or listeners; main tasks still 1 tap; rows do not move under a finger (Preview only, simulated). Needs work: staff-first Home shows 0 of 5 coworker rows until Got it (the head chef's call); Prep drops from 6 to 5 rows on days with no band; Headspace, because there are two ways to put it away and 'heads-up' is untested with new starters; and the clipped 'Do not prep' breaks the rule that every state has words. text:
Score 8 (A 7). Endorse with changes. The mix hangs together: one Home slot (card, then line), one work-page slot, and a tag inside Orders. It beats A. B's open-only rule closes my top A risk (0 px moves, 16 simulated checks). The Orders tag targets missed stock. C's card answers A's passivity without the bell dot, receipts or a card above Your day. Cost: 0 of 5 coworker rows until Got it, and 4 Got its for Ann this week.

New failure paths:
1. The locked slot cuts off words. On Prep at 390, a booking or cancellation arrives while the page is open, with a 37-character name. The words need 90 px in the 50 px slot and 'Do not prep' is hidden. Reproduced (prep.html).
2. After the first Got it, the bottom slip covers 18 of the 48 px of the next card's Got it, and Undo touches Open the function. Reproduced (home.html, 390).
3. The red Cancelled card reaches only people who tapped Got it, though the line told everyone. Risk, Not evidenced.

Changes: put the must-read words in the one-line label and cut the name short, with a long-name and large-text test. Answer Got it in the line's place. No Tomorrow card after a week Got it (4 to 2 taps). Cancelled stays on the line until the date. Design the busy-week card first. Test open-only on the real paint().

Contract fit: Needs work. Colours and reads work. Staff-first order, Prep 6 to 5 rows and two ways to put it away need the head chef. All Preview.

changes: Replace 'Function heads-up' with plain words a second-language speaker knows, such as 'Function this week' on the week card and 'Function tomorrow' on the day-before card, then test it with a new starter.
Day-before card foot: 'The day before, once for everyone. Got it is just for you.' reads as a contradiction. Say 'Everyone sees this once, the day before. Got it hides it only for you.'
Show that the Next function line opens something: a chevron on Home, where there is room, and on the work pages if it still fits the fixed 50 px slot. Today only the card has 'Open the function'.
Keep the slip clear of the second card's Got it after the first Got it. Lift the slip or scroll card 2's Got it fully into view, so the next step is not half hidden.

Before ready: a new-starter walk-through of Got it (Home, per person, until the day before) against the minus (work pages, this phone, until tomorrow), the two-staff shared tablet click test, and a design for 3 or more functions in one week.
newRisks: The slip 'Got it. Smith 60th stays as one line on Home.' covers about half of the Jones wedding card's Got it button at 390 px until it goes. Reproduced in the static preview, shots/home-after-390.png. Impact low: friction, Undo sits on the other side.

Cards in sequence: a second card opens in the same place, so a quick reader may think Got it did not work. A double tap is safe: the second tap lands on the Platters row, not a button. Checked in the mix preview screenshots (home-390.png, home-after-390.png). Whether a new starter understands it: Risk, Not evidenced.

Two put-away controls with different reach, new to the mix (A had no Got it, C had no minus). On a shared tablet the minus also hides the line for the next person signed in that day. Words checked in the mix preview (minus.spokenLabel and the slip). Understanding and handover: Risk, Not evidenced.
Busy week: one Got it per function per stage, so 4 this week for Ann and 5 cards in a row with 5 functions. Risk, Not evidenced (no design for it yet).
contractFit: Needs work. Staff-first Home: Your day stays first at 169 px. Until Got it, the card sits between Your day and On with you, and 0 of 5 coworker rows show at 390. That departure needs the head chef's OK. Words and states mostly Work: every state has words, Cancelled has a strike, the word and a plain button, and the Orders tag uses ink words at 13.48:1. 'Heads-up' is still open. Focus rings, dark mode, large text, 360 px and every Implemented app measurement are Not evidenced. All numbers are Preview.
text:
Score 8 (A 6, B 5, C 7). Endorse with changes. The mix is one coherent flow. Each person reads every fact once on Home, with 0 taps. Got it folds the card in place into the same Next function line the work pages use, so a reflex tap no longer loses the function (checked: the line's top is 389 px, the same as the card's). It beats C: the bell dot is gone, Your day stays first, and Cancelled has words and a plain button.

Changes: 1. Replace "Function heads-up" with plain words, such as "Function this week" and "Function tomorrow". 2. Day-before foot: "Everyone sees this once, the day before. Got it hides it only for you." 3. Show that the line opens: a chevron, where it fits. 4. Keep the slip clear of the second card's Got it.

New failure paths: the slip covers half of card 2's Got it (Reproduced, home-after-390.png). A second card in the same place can look like Got it failed. A double tap lands on Platters, not a button (Checked in the mix screenshots). Got it versus the minus, and a minus on the tablet carrying over to the next person (Risk, Not evidenced). Five functions means five Got its (Risk).

Contract fit: Needs work. The card sits between Your day and On with you, with 0 of 5 coworker rows at 390 until Got it, which needs the head chef's OK. Focus, dark mode, large text and the implemented app: Not evidenced.

bestSingle: A (Fill the gap), my earlier 7. The mix keeps everything I recommended with A: B's open-only slot (Checked in mix preview, 0 px move in 16 checks), B's in-line Orders tag, no bell dot, no receipts. It adds C's once-per-person heads-up card under Your day, which collapses in place to A's line. That gives a real attention moment with every fact at 0 taps, and still adds no read, write, rule or listener.
changes: Apply the open-only rule to the Home slot as well, in PR 2. homePaint() in js/prep.js redraws each Home part whenever its HTML changes, on every functions paint (js/functions.js paint(), every 20 s and on every listener change) and on the 30 s cut-off tick. So a Booked today, Changed or next-stage card would be inserted live and drop On with you about 331 px while someone is reading it. New or returning cards wait for the next Home open. Only the words of a card already on screen change in place. Add a click test: a booking arrives with Home open and the top of On with you does not move.

Define exactly what counts as an 'open' for the lock: a route change, the app becoming visible again, a PIN unlock after an idle or daily lock, and a reload. Also say that a function today (a same-day booking with rounds) breaks the lock and draws the full band, because a missed round is the mistake the band exists to stop (service rule 3). Draw and test that state.

Size the fixed slot when the page opens for the tallest set of its words at the current text size (boot.js text size, the stand-in fonts). Put the status word first (Cancelled, Order today, Tomorrow, No signal) so it is never clipped. Today the words are 49 px in a 50 px slot with the preview fonts.

Give the line's minus its own day key (for example lk.fn.ahead.fold), not the band's lk.fn.fold. With the shared key, hiding next week's line also folds an Order today or Tomorrow band that appears later the same day.

lk.fn.hu.<staffId>: store the function id, the stage and a now() stamp. Treat a function as Changed when it has chg[] entries newer than that stamp (chg already holds up to 8 entries, so this needs no read). Prune entries for past days when Home paints, and say in a comment what makes the key out of date, as the saved-copy rule requires.
Keep the slip (toast) off the second card's actions at 390 px. Either raise the slip or scroll the next card's Got it into view.
newRisks: The Home slot is redrawn live. homePaint() runs on every functions paint and every cut-off tick, so without its own lock a card arriving mid-view pushes On with you and its 'View today's full team' link down under a finger. The card's innerHTML can also be replaced while a finger is on Got it. A and B had no Home card and C had none under Your day, so this is new to the mix. Evidence: Risk / Not evidenced, from a source read of js/prep.js homePaint() and js/functions.js paint().

The open-only lock now holds the band's shared slot, which B never locked (B locked only its own in-list line). A short-notice Order today or Tomorrow booking, or a same-day booking, that arrives while a shared tablet sits on Prep shows only as 50 px of words. The full band with its platters, rounds and pinned strip waits for the next open, which may not come until the 04:00 reload, and later still if unsent work blocks that reload. Evidence: the Order today words for a booking that arrives while Prep is open were Checked in the mix preview (prep-390-booking-while-open.png). The same-day case and the tablet left open all day are Risk / Not evidenced. The words for a same-day booking are not drawn.

The fixed-height words fit 49 px of a 50 px slot with the preview fonts. With the large text setting or the app's stand-in fonts they must either be clipped (and could lose 'Do not prep') or grow and break the lock. Evidence: Risk / Not evidenced (measurements.json openOnly wordsHeight 49).

After the first Got it, the slip covers the lower part of the Jones card's Got it and Open the function at 390 px. That card runs to 762 px, the slip starts at about 710 px and the tab bar at 776 px. C placed the card above Your day, so its next card did not sit under the slip. Evidence: Reproduced in the mix preview screenshot shots/home-after-390.png. A double tap on Got it lands on the Jones card's text, not its Got it (by screenshot positions; the tap was not exercised).
contractFit: Reads: Works. There are no new reads, writes, rules or listeners. The functions listener at js/functions.js line 329 (kq from today, limit 150) already holds every upcoming function, the Orders tag uses od from that same list, and Changed words come from the function's existing chg[] list. Saved copies: Needs work. The new lk.fn.hu.<staffId> key needs a comment on what makes it out of date and pruning of past days, and the minus should not share lk.fn.fold. Service continuity: Needs work and the head chef's call. Prep goes from 6 to 5 rows at 390 px on band-empty days, and Home shows 0 of 5 coworker rows until Got it. Both are Preview figures, to be remeasured in the implemented app with the real shell, the mascot, the cut-off bar and large text. State meaning and surfaces: Works in the preview (quiet paper, ink tag, no green Saved). Focus rings, dark variants and large text: Not evidenced. A mock cannot prove the per-person keying, the midnight repaint or role gating. Those need click tests with the stand-in clock, two staff on one device and rows in tests/roles.test.js.
text:
Mix 8 (A 7, C 5, B 4). It beats A: C's card gives each person every fact at 0 taps, and my repairs stay (open-only slot, Orders tag, no bell dot, no receipts). No new reads, writes, rules or listeners: the functions listener holds every function; chg[] gives Changed words. Cost: 4 pull requests.

Endorse with changes:
1. Lock the Home slot too. homePaint() redraws Home every 20 s, so a new card drops On with you 331 px mid-view. Cards wait for the next open.
2. Define "opened": route change, return to the app, PIN unlock, reload. A function today breaks the lock.
3. Size the slot for the tallest words at the current text size.
4. The line's minus gets its own day key, not lk.fn.fold, so it never folds a later Order today or Tomorrow band.
5. lk.fn.hu.<staffId>: id, stage, now() stamp; prune past days.
6. Keep the slip off the second card's Got it.

New risks: Home repaint (Risk, source read); a tablet left on Prep keeps 50 px words until 04:00 (booking Checked in mix preview, same-day Risk); 49 of 50 px clipped at large text (Risk); slip over Jones's Got it (Reproduced, home-after-390.png).

Contract fit: reads Works; saved copies, service continuity Needs work; focus, dark, large text Not evidenced.

bestSingle: C (my round 2 score 7). The mix keeps C's 0-tap card but puts it under Your day. After Got it, the card becomes A's line in the same spot instead of dropping back to 998 px. It also adds A's work-page reach without C's bell dot.
changes: After the first Got it at 390, the slip covers about the lower third of the next card's Got it (slip top about 709 px, Jones Got it about 679 to 725 px, home-after-390.png). Either scroll the next card's Got it clear of the slip, or put Undo inside the collapsed line.
Draw and measure the busy-week card (3 or more functions, one Got it) before build. One card at a time keeps On with you below the first screen until the last Got it (737 / 780 px).
On a shared device, reset the work-page minus when a different person signs in. The line is redrawn at page open after the PIN, so the open-only rule still holds.

Before ready, check in the implemented app: keyboard focus rings, dark variants, large text, 360 px, the head chef's cut-off bar with the line (A measured 118 px, 4 rows) and the mascot. Also measure the Order today tag inside the strip, which is missing from the contrast list.
Add the booking-while-open word swap to the header-height click test: the first row stays put, and a tap opens the function the words name.
newRisks: The slip covers the next heads-up card's Got it after the first Got it at 390, so its visible target shrinks to about 30 px. Reproduced (Preview, shots/home-after-390.png).

A booking confirmed mid-view swaps the slot's words from 'Smith 60th' to 'Order today · Stock: Lee engagement' under a finger. A tap aimed at Smith opens Lee, and the nearer function goes unnamed on that work page until the next open. The 0 px height is Checked in the mix preview (prep-390-booking-while-open.png). The mis-tap and the missing name are Risk, Not evidenced.

Sequential cards keep On with you off the first screen across every Got it in a week. Checked in the mix preview for two functions (0 of 5 coworker rows until the last Got it). A 5-function week is Risk, Not evidenced.
On a shared tablet, one person's minus hides the line for the next person that day. This undercuts 'everyone's attention'. Risk, Not evidenced (spec break-it 3).
contractFit: Surface purpose: Works. The card is quiet paper with a steel edge and the line is reference paper; upcoming functions are never charcoal or amber. State meaning: Works. Orange appears only on Got it. Cancelled uses red with the word and a strike, and its button is the plain .btn. Real contrast: Works for text (lowest 4.86:1) and control edges. Focus, dark, large text and 360 px are Not evidenced. Staff-first Home: Needs the head chef's OK, because 0 of 5 coworker rows show at 390 until Got it. Service continuity: Needs work, because Prep goes from 6 to 5 rows on band-empty days. All figures are Preview.
text:
Score 8, which beats C (my best single design, 7). Endorse with changes.

It reads as one design: attention once on Home and a quiet reminder everywhere else. Your day stays first at 169 px. The card collapses to the line in the same spot (389 px), so the function never drops back to 998 px. The two put-away controls never share a page, the line is the same on every page, and the open-only rule held at 0 px across 16 checks. Coming up drops Smith 60th, so the function is not shown three times.

Changes:
1. After the first Got it at 390, the slip covers the lower third of Jones's Got it (about 709 px against 679 to 725 px). Scroll the button clear or put Undo in the line.
2. Draw the card for a week with three or more functions before the build.
3. On a shared device, reset the minus when a different person signs in.
4. Test focus rings, dark mode, large text, 360 px, and the cut-off bar with the line.

New failure paths:
- The slip over the next Got it: Reproduced (Preview, home-after-390.png).
- A booking that arrives mid-view swaps the slot from Smith 60th to Lee engagement under a finger. Height: Checked in the mix preview. Mis-tap: Risk, Not evidenced.
- Cards one at a time keep On with you off the first screen until the last Got it. Checked for two functions; a busy week is a Risk.

Contract fit: surfaces and states Work, lowest text contrast 4.86:1. Staff-first Home and the lost Prep row need the head chef's OK.
